name: LiveBench
intro: LiveBench 是一个动态、版本化且污染受限的大模型基准。它从近期信息源构造新题，也把既有任务改得更难；每题必须有可核验的客观真值并由任务专用程序自动评分，不依赖人类或 LLM 偏好 Judge。论文与在线基准持续演化，任何规模和榜单结果都必须绑定具体发布日期。
org: Abacus.AI, New York University, NVIDIA, University of Maryland, USC, Columbia University
build_method: 近期来源采集与程序化生成、既有任务加难、自动与人工质检、版本化周期更新
metric: 逐题 0–1 任务专用客观得分；逐题均值到任务、任务等权均值到类别、类别等权均值到 LiveBench 总分
task_type: 选择题, 开放式问答, 代码生成, 补全, 软件工程代理
eval_feature: 动态, 特定版本, 污染受限, 客观自动评分, 零样本
scale: 论文 v2 快照：18 个任务、6 个类别，首次更新后 1,000 题；官网 2026-06-25 公开成本快照的标准有效基数：23 个任务列、7 个类别、1,270 题（1,198 常规 + 72 Agentic Coding v2）
task_type_en: Multiple Choice, Open-ended QA, Code Generation, Completion, Software-engineering Agents
build_method_en: Recent-source Collection, Procedural Generation, Harder Task Variants, Automated and Manual QC, Versioned Periodic Refresh
eval_feature_en: Dynamic, Release-specific, Contamination-limited, Objective Automatic Scoring, Zero-shot
intro_en: LiveBench is a dynamic, versioned, contamination-limited LLM benchmark. It constructs questions from recent information sources and harder variants of existing tasks; every question must have verifiable objective ground truth and a task-specific automatic evaluator, without a human- or LLM-preference judge. Because both the paper suite and live leaderboard evolve, every scale and score must be tied to a dated release.
scale_en: Paper v2 snapshot: 18 tasks across 6 categories and 1,000 questions after the first update; the official site's public 2026-06-25 cost snapshot encodes a canonical active basis of 23 task columns, 7 categories, and 1,270 questions (1,198 regular + 72 Agentic Coding v2)
metric_en: Task-specific objective per-question scores in [0, 1]; question mean to task, equal task mean to category, and equal category mean to the LiveBench score

evidence.supports: Two construction source types; objective-ground-truth gate; 18 tasks and 6 categories; 40-100 questions per paper task; prompt formatting; 1,000-question updated snapshot; monthly roughly one-sixth replacement; one-month withholding; grading QC; temperature-zero single-turn experiments; task/category/overall aggregation

Eleven accepted release dates through 2026-06-25; release/removal-date filtering; a base temperature fallback of zero whose effective request value can differ through model api_kwargs, question, CLI, and provider configuration paths (model configs include 0.7 and 1.0); task-specific evaluator dispatch and standard-parser QC; evaluation status; Mini-SWE-Agent and Docker agentic-coding path with separate infrastructure/flaky retry-or-skip handling; question-to-task-to-category aggregation

Official 2026-06-25 release selector; 23 task columns in 7 categories; Agentic Coding split into JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python; release-specific score aggregation; public cost snapshot question counts and its canonical 1,198 regular plus 72 agentic basis
Twenty-three nq_* task columns; canonical active/scored basis of 1,270 questions for complete rows. The deployed file is byte-identical to the file at the pinned official modern-site commit

evidence.supports: Public-data boundary: the six paper-era category datasets are public, while the current official site's newest question batch and complete 2026 release corpus are not exposed there

paper_v2_snapshot.update_policy: Monthly in the paper; replace about one sixth on average; prioritize oldest, easiest, or suspected-contaminated tasks; withhold new questions for one month

official_site_release_2026_06_25.question_count_scope: Encoded by the public cost snapshot's nq_* columns and pinned generator as the canonical active basis; individual model rows can be lower when scored judgments are missing, and this does not reveal the exact current private subset
official_site_release_2026_06_25.refresh_statement: Questions are updated regularly so the benchmark completely refreshes every six months

not_publicly_specified: Complete current 2026 question corpus and exact current private-question count
Question-generation code for the private refresh pipeline
Exact replacement fraction for each post-paper release

One universal current decoding temperature or a single cross-provider precedence contract; pinned code has a base fallback of 0, while model api_kwargs, question, CLI, and provider configuration paths can produce effective values including 0.7 and 1.0

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2406.19314v2, official code commit 4bf3d6f4cb37fa8dc3967dd1b124fef5d4099635, modern-site source commit f2e0b4bcffae54c84461d96fc8e668c4b57a0627, the deployed 2026-06-25 cost snapshot, and pinned public Hugging Face category revisions. The paper builds 18 tasks in six categories from recent information sources or harder and more diverse variants, admits only verifiable objective ground truth, writes task-specific parseable-answer prompts, validates questions, and reaches 1,000 questions after its first update. Its maintenance policy updates monthly, replaces about one sixth on average, prioritizes old/easy/suspected-contaminated tasks, changes generation scripts to make distributions harder, reruns models, and delays new-question release by one month. The deployed official site is a later dated contract: LiveBench-2026-06-25 exposes 23 task columns across seven categories, including Agentic Coding, and states a full refresh about every six months. Its public cost snapshot and pinned generator encode a canonical active basis of 1,270 questions—1,198 regular and 72 Agentic Coding v2—although individual model rows can contain fewer scored judgments and the exact private subset remains undisclosed. Fixed code selects questions using release and removal dates. For standard inference it starts from a temperature fallback of 0, but the effective request can differ through model api_kwargs, question, CLI, and provider configuration paths; pinned model configs include 0.7 and 1.0, so 0 is not a universal current model temperature. Standard objective scorers alone feed the paper-derived manual parser-QC loop. Current agentic coding instead runs Mini-SWE-Agent, Docker, repository patches, and tests, and performs its own infrastructure/flaky retry-or-skip handling before the two judgment branches merge. Scores remain per-question values in [0,1], averaged equally from questions to tasks, tasks to categories, and categories to the release-specific overall score. Public code and older HF data do not equal the withheld full current release, and different releases must not be merged as one fixed benchmark.
